metadata.note: The Gulf, Mobile and Northern (Jan 1917 - Sept 13, 1940) and the GM&O-era continuation of its passenger service, plus two small predecessors drawn as their own companies: the Meridian and Memphis (1914-1923) and the Jackson and Eastern (1924-1926). Rule 4 splits: every GM&N feature with GM&O-era service is split at the Sept 13, 1940 merger into a GM&O feature on identical geometry; M&M -> GM&N at the 1923 lease (not the 1918 stock control); J&E -> GM&N at the July 1, 1926 lease. Pre-1917 MJ&KC / Gulf and Chicago / NOM&C years and pre-July-1933 New Orleans Great Northern years belong to other layers and are not drawn here.
sources: Lemly, James H., The Gulf, Mobile and Ohio (1953), https://acmeme.com/gmo/
Official Guide, March 1940, GM&N pp. 610-611, page images at https://www.american-rails.com/gmn.html
metadata.geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror, traced with opstrace.py on ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O; Slidell - New Orleans on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern (NS NO&NE District). OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the Richton - Bay Springs gap and returned nothing.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] start years: gmn-mobile-union and gmn-union-middleton 1919 (GM&N took over Jan 1917; 1917-18 passenger service near-certain but unproven); gmn-middleton-jackson-tn 1922 (line opened Sept 2, 1919; 1919-22 passenger service probable, unproven); gmn-dyersburg-branch 1938 (GM&N operator from 1924 or 1927 - source conflict - but no passenger evidence before the Dec 1938 timetable).

[OPEN] end years: gmo-mobile-union 1942 (only the Mobile Rebel's Apr 28, 1942 cut-off is dated; later local/mixed service unknown either way); gmn-blodgett-branch 1921-1924 (both ends open; true span within 1918-1935).
[ANCHOR] single years: gmn-bogue-chitto-branch 1935 and gmn-shore-line 1935 - when rail passengers gave way to the Gulf Transport buses shown by Dec 1939 is unknown.

GM&O-era passenger service on the Meridian and Dyersburg branches after Sept 1940: none confirmed, so neither is drawn after 1940. Lemly ch. XVI's Dec 1951 removal of 'local trains from Jackson, Tennessee, to Meridian' does not name the route.
The Rebel's exact 1954 end date, and whether Slidell - New Orleans was cut first (8 March 1954, single unread photo caption).
NOGN -> GM&N split date on Jackson, Miss. - New Orleans: 1933 lease used here vs 1930 'Louisiana Division' (Lemly ch. VIII).
Union - Lena under the GM&N, July 1926 - July 1927: passenger service not established, not drawn.
Headways and speeds are estimates except where a segment note quotes a timetable (Rebel 1939, Dyersburg mixed 1938).
metadata.omitted: Hattiesburg Branch and Ellisville Branch (no confirmable GM&N passenger year); GM&O-era Meridian and Dyersburg branches (no confirmed GM&O passenger year); Paducah trackage rights, Chickasaw spur and Columbia - West Columbia (freight or bus only) - see the research report.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 179.9 mi against a documented 181 mi (Mar 1940 Official Guide 'Union and Mobile'; Fowler 180.8). Traced over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O: the active CN Beaumont Subdivision north from Mobile and the abandoned grade north of it. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS (3, 2.9 mi total) where the mapped abandoned grade breaks: south of Richton 1.5 mi, through Laurel 0.9 mi, near Sandersville 0.5 mi. The Mobile end stops where the mapped ex-GM&N track ends south of downtown (about 2.7 km from the city centre); the approach to the GM&N's Conception St. / Government St. passenger station is not verified. LATER ALIGNMENT: the corridor as it survives or is mapped as abandoned today, not a verified 1919-1942 alignment.

segments.note: START IS [OPEN]: 1919 is the earliest CONFIRMED year of passenger service under this operator (Fowler's 'b: 1919GMNt' timetable letter covers the whole Mobile - Middleton line; the GM&N took over an operating passenger railroad in Jan 1917, so 1917-18 is near-certain but unproven), not a known beginning. Service probably began earlier, but no source proves it. Do not move the start earlier without evidence. The end is the GM&N/M&O merger of Sept 13, 1940, not a service end - service continues as feature gmo-mobile-union. GM&N's own line, built by the Mobile, Jackson and Kansas City 1898-1906 (pre-1917 years belong to that company's layer). Through Mobile - Jackson, Tenn. trains first ran Oct 15, 1922, with Frisco-GM&N Memphis - Mobile Pullmans from Dec 1, 1922 (Lemly ch. VI). Mar 1932 - Mar 1933 day trains were cut back to Laurel while night trains kept running; no gap in rail service (Lemly ch. X). The 'Mobile Rebel' shuttle Union - Mobile entered service Jan 1938 (Lemly ch. XI), timetabled as 1-21/22-2 on Dec 20, 1938 (Mar 1940 Guide). Headway 1440 = the single Mobile Rebel round trip of the 1938-40 timetable; earlier frequencies not sourced. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: dates and service from Fowler MS station list line 55 legend 'b: 1919GMNt', the Mar 1940 Official Guide p.611 'Union and Mobile' table, and Lemly, The Gulf, Mobile and Ohio (1953) ch. VI, X, XI.

Jackson, Miss. - Slidell: 150.9 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O (CN Bogalusa Subdivision and abandoned grade), no straight legs; the two traces meet at Slidell with a 0.34 mi straight join. Slidell - New Orleans (26.9 mi traced) is TRACKAGE RIGHTS over ANOTHER COMPANY'S TRACK: the Southern Railway's New Orleans and Northeastern, drawn on the present NS NO&NE District (old_railway_operator=Southern) across the Lake Pontchartrain trestle to the junction at Almonaster/Press St. STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: the final 2.8 mi from there to the site of New Orleans Terminal Station (Canal and Basin streets; station closed 1954, approach tracks lifted) is a straight line, not the historical approach route. The Southern track (about 27 mi) belongs to another company and is drawn here only because GM&N/GM&O trains ran over it. LATER ALIGNMENT: corridor as mapped today; the 1930s-1950s lake-trestle alignment was not separately verified.

segments.note: Ex New Orleans Great Northern (the GM&N's Louisiana Division). The start is the operator change, not the start of service: the reorganized NOGN Railway was leased to the GM&N effective July 1, 1933 (ICC approval Aug 1, 1933; Lemly ch. XXI). Service was continuous from NOGN days; the pre-July-1933 years belong to the NOGN layer. SOURCE CONFLICT: Lemly ch. VIII says after Feb 1930 'the line then became the Louisiana Division of the GM&N', which could argue for 1930; ch. XXI has the NOGN in its own receivership Nov 7, 1932 and leased only July 1, 1933. 1933 is used here. Rail passenger service under the GM&N is confirmed for 1934 (night trains New Orleans - Jackson, Tenn., until the Rebels replaced them) and 1935-1940 (THE REBEL, in service June/July 1935 - Lemly ch. XI). The end is the GM&N/M&O merger of Sept 13, 1940, not a service end; service continues under the GM&O as the companion gmo- feature on identical geometry. Slidell - New Orleans (~35 mi) was TRACKAGE RIGHTS over the Southern Railway's New Orleans and Northeastern - another company's track. Headway 1440 = THE REBEL Nos. 1/2 only south of Jackson, Miss. in the Dec 16, 1939 table; other years unsourced. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Lemly ch. XXI (lease, July 1, 1933) and ch. XI (night trains, the Rebel 1935); Mar 1940 Official Guide p.611; Fowler LA line 8 (operated over SOU).

segments.note: GM&O-era continuation from the Sept 13, 1940 GM&N/M&O merger. THE REBEL Nos. 1/2, Jackson, Tenn. - Union - Jackson, Miss. - New Orleans: confirmed by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (GM&O Table 4, Jan 13, 1952, equipment list naming 'TRAIN 1 - THE REBEL Jackson, Tenn., to New Orleans' with a drawing-room observation sleeper) and the April 1953 Official Guide (streamlinerschedules). The 1954 end is the discontinuance year given by secondary sources (Wikipedia 'Gulf Coast Rebel': 'The GM&O discontinued the original Rebels in 1954'; MDAH marker: service to the Jackson depot 'ended in 1954'; chicagorailfan) - the exact date is not established. An unread photo caption claims Slidell - New Orleans was cut on 8 March 1954, still within 1954. Not to be confused with the Gulf Coast Rebel (St. Louis - Mobile over the ex-M&O main line). The Rebel's 1941-1949 extension north of Jackson, Tenn. ran on ex-M&O track and is not part of this layer. Headway 1440 = the single Rebel round trip of the 1952-53 timetables. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Feb 1952 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, equipment list ~lines 125401-125530 and Table 4 ~lines 125991-126080); April 1953 Official Guide via streamlinerschedules; end year from Wikipedia, MDAH marker and chicagorailfan (secondary).

segments.note: Ex Meridian and Memphis. Start = operator change: 'In 1923, separate operation of the Meridian and Memphis ceased and the GM&N operated this mileage under lease' (Lemly ch. V); a GM&N Louisville - Meridian train started June 1923 (ch. VI). Aug 1924 the GM&N's second gasoline motor car was 'running twice daily between Meridian and Union' (ch. VI, VII). Dec 20, 1938 table: gas-electric 6-15/16-5 daily, through from Jackson, Miss. via Union (Mar 1940 Guide p.610). End = Sept 13, 1940 merger. No GM&O-era passenger service on this branch is confirmed (the Feb 1952 Guide index lists Duffee without a timetable), so nothing is drawn after 1940 - that is a withheld unknown, not a known end. Headway 1440 = one daily train in 1938-40; the 1924 twice-daily motor car would be 720. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Lemly ch. V, VI, VII; Mar 1940 Official Guide p.610 'Meridian Branch'; Fowler MS line 58.

segments.note: First 30 mi ready June 30, 1913; into Union Dec 1913; 15,741 passengers in the fiscal year ending June 30, 1914 (Lemly ch. XX) - 1914 is the first year proven by passenger figures, the 1913 opening month is not. Steam passenger trains still running in 1921 (Lemly ch. VI). GM&N stock control from Jan 1918 did NOT change the operator - 'separate operation' continued to 1923, when the GM&N took over operation under lease; service continued as gmn-meridian-branch. Headway 1440 is an estimate; no M&M timetable read.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 48.4 mi against a documented 48 mi (Mar 1940 Guide; Fowler 48.5). No straight-line legs; all on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O (West Tennessee Railroad and abandoned grade). LATER ALIGNMENT: corridor as mapped today.

segments.note: START IS [OPEN]: 1938 is the earliest CONFIRMED year of passenger service under this operator (the Dec 20, 1938 'Dyersburg Branch' table in the Mar 1940 Official Guide p.610: trains 433/434, defined on the page as 'Mixed train', daily except Sunday, Dyersburg - Bells - Jackson, Tenn., 48 mi), not a known beginning. Service probably began earlier, but no source proves it. Do not move the start earlier without evidence. A mixed train carried passengers, so this counts as passenger service. The GM&N became operator of the ex-Birmingham and Northwestern in 1924 (Lemly ch. V) or March 1927 (Lemly ch. XX) - SOURCE CONFLICT, unresolved; GM&N passenger service between then and 1938 is unsourced. End = Sept 13, 1940 merger; no GM&O-era passenger service is confirmed (Feb 1952 Guide index lists Crockett Mills and Friendship without a timetable), so nothing is drawn after 1940 - a withheld unknown, not a known end. Headway 1440 = one mixed train each way, daily except Sunday. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Mar 1940 Official Guide p.610 'Dyersburg Branch' (Dec 20, 1938); Lemly ch. V, XX.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 24.5 mi against a documented 24.4 mi (Fowler MS line 56; Lemly 'about 25'). No straight-line legs; follows the OSM abandoned grade tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O (named 'Blodgett Branch' in part). segments.note: BOTH ENDS ARE [OPEN]. 1921 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year ('STEAM TRAINS on the Blodgett branch and the Meridian branch have been replaced with motor trains for passenger service since the inspection trip of 1921', Lemly ch. VI); the first 18 mi McLain - Avera opened Aug 3, 1918 (ch. XXII) and passenger service may have begun then, unproven. 1924 is the last CONFIRMED year (gasoline motor car installed 1923 and still described c.1924, carrying passengers, mail and express - ch. VI, VII), NOT a known end. The branch was abandoned and dismantled in 1935 (ch. XI) - an abandonment date, not a passenger end. The true span lies somewhere within 1918-1935; no source dates when passenger service started or stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 1440 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Lemly ch. I, VI, VII, XI, XXII; Fowler MS line 56.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] - a single proven year. Lemly ch. XI: the Traffic Department 'would place a railplane in service between Jackson, Mississippi, and Tylertown, Mississippi, on January 6 [1935]'; 'The railplane was also serving on the Louisiana Division line from Jackson, Mississippi, to Tylertown.' Rail passenger service under the GM&N (operator from the July 1, 1933 lease) certainly ran wider than 1935 both ways, but no other year is confirmed. By Dec 16, 1939 the Guide shows only a Gulf Transport BUS table Tylertown - Franklinton - Bogalusa, which proves a bus existed, not that rail had ended. Only Rio - Tylertown is drawn here; the railplane's run north of Rio used the main line (gmn-jackson-ms-new-orleans). Do not widen or delete this anchor. Headway 1440 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Lemly ch. XI; Fowler LA line 10; Mar 1940 Official Guide p.611 (bus table, context only).
